context.problem_statement: Fit a multiple linear regression model to predict compressive strength of concrete based on its composition. Features: cement, water, fly_ash, superplasticizer, coarse_aggregate, age_days. Target: compressive_strength_MPa. Steps: (1) fit OLS regression using statsmodels, (2) report R-squared and adjusted R-squared, (3) report coefficients with standard errors, t-statistics, and p-values, (4) perform residual diagnostics: plot residuals vs fitted values, compute Durbin-Watson statistic for autocorrelation, test normality of residuals with Shapiro-Wilk test, (5) identify and report statistically significant predictors (p < 0.05).
context.expert_knowledge: Use statsmodels.api.OLS(y, sm.add_constant(X)).fit(). R-squared = 1 - SS_res/SS_tot. Adjusted R-squared penalizes for extra predictors. Durbin-Watson statistic near 2 = no autocorrelation; < 1 or > 3 is problematic. Shapiro-Wilk p > 0.05 indicates normal residuals. Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) detects multicollinearity. Condition number > 30 indicates potential multicollinearity.
